description.narrative: Several governmental and social partners' organizations have substantially increased their capacity to undertake analyses of market demand for skilled workforce and on demand-driven planning of TVET applying ILO's methodology. The ILO provided training on TVET and labour market data collation and analysis to a total of 335 representatives of constituents' organizations during the biennium.

description.narrative:
The Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) increased its capacity to design and implement STEM learning in TVET; 185 TVET Trainers were trained in the development of STEM in TVET Curriculum Guide and STEM in TVET Trainers Training (April 2021).
TESDA and TVET institutions also increased their capacity to provide online job readiness training for young people, particularly underprivileged women through Online Job Readiness Training, reaching 700 women and providing training to 100 TVET Trainers (October 2021). The ILO provided technical support to TESDA and TVET providers. It also trained employees from ECOP Member Companies online for In Business Soft Skills Training, and updated the manual for Community-Based Training as tool for Community Training and Education Coordinators.

description.narrative:
The Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) published Skills Needs Anticipation (SNA) reports for the Information Technology and Business Process Management (IT BPM) and Construction sectors, and has carried forward the application of the ILO SNA methodology to two additional sectors (Logistics and Health).
A team of TESDA Technical Staff is now able to manage the SNA process and translate the report results to inform TESDA plans and programs.
Tripartite constituents and other strategic partners have increased appreciation of SNA.
A Guidance Manual on SNA was drafted to institutionalize the methodology along with other TESDA processes for anticipating future skills needs. TESDA Circular 042-2021 already incorporates and recognizes SNA as a key process and methodology in the implementation of area-based and demand-driven TVET. Responding to TESDA's request, the ILO supported the application of SNA in specific sectors. In the pilot implementation of SNA methodology to complement existing skills anticipation methods in TESDA, this was applied in two sectors - ITBPM and Construction (INSIGHT 2)
Key TESDA Staff capacitated on the SNA methodology. Tripartite constituents and other strategic partners on skills development were introduced to SNA uses. (INSIGHT 2)
